title: Optimize walkthrough - quantization profiles (INT8 vs FP8)
next_steps: Send INT8/FP8 benchmark spreadsheet and raw logs
Schedule 2-hr pilot run on Dedicated with their 512-token workload
Share security and SOC2 docs and architecture diagram
action_items: Samir Patel: Run quantization repro on Redwood Optimize with Orion sample prompts (due: 2025-02-19)
Jordan Lee: Share pricing for Dedicated pilot + estimated token costs (due: 2025-02-14)
Maria Gomez: Provide 3 representative prompt sets and expected quality thresholds (due: 2025-02-17)
header:
Date: 2025-02-12
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Alyssa Chen (Redwood Product), Maria Gomez (Orion Head of ML), Ethan Zhao (Orion SRE), Priya Raman (Orion Product), Luke Turner (Orion CTO)
summary: Redwood Optimize walkthrough focused on quantization profiles (INT8 vs FP8) and tradeoffs between output quality and latency/cost. Reviewed benchmark methodology, showed live demos of INT8 and FP8 on a trimmed 512-token clinical summarization prompt set, discussed degradation modes, fallback strategies, and next steps for pilot on Dedicated capacity.
transcript:
[15:00] Jordan Lee: All right everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Jordan from Redwood, I'll kick us off.
[15:07] Maria Gomez: Hi, thanks. We're excited to see the quantization stuff—our main ask is how much perf we can get without breaking clinical accuracy.
[15:14] Samir Patel: Great, so today's walk is Optimize's quantization profiles, we'll compare INT8 and FP8, show latency and BLEU/Rouge-style tradeoffs, and talk about fallback options. Quick note: some transcripts may say 'quantisation' cause the engine sometimes uses UK spelling.
[15:28] Ethan Zhao: sounds good, our SRE cares about peak p95 latency and cold start behaviors.
[15:34] Alyssa Chen: I'll share a short deck and then demo two runs, same model family, one INT8, one FP8. We also have a batching config that affects numbers so we'll keep it consistent.
[15:46] Jordan Lee: quick qual question—what's your typical prompt length and the payload distribution?
[15:51] Maria Gomez: mostly 400–600 tokens on clinical notes summarization, but we also have 50–100 token triage prompts.
[15:57] Priya Raman: timeline wise, target pilot in next 2–3 weeks if results look good.
[16:02] Samir Patel: perfect. I'll start the demo — sharing my screen.
[16:15] Samir Patel: first chart is latency vs token for FP16 baseline, FP8, INT8 across 256/512/1024 seq lengths. Notice FP8 sits close to FP16 on quality but gives ~1.2x speedup in our P100-ish tests, INT8 gives ~2.5x speedup but some quality drop.
[16:32] Luke Turner: when you say "quality drop" can you quantify? like how much ROUGE or hallucination risk?
[16:37] Samir Patel: yes, for our clinical prompt set: FP8 average ROUGE-L delta is ~-0.7 points vs FP16, INT8 is ~-2.8 points in one-shot summarization. Hallucination rate measured by our eval harness increased 0.5% for FP8 and ~2.3% for INT8 on the lab set.
[16:55] Maria Gomez: 2.3% hallucination is big for us. What's the failure mode—does it create dangerous fabrications or just small paraphrase drift?
[17:02] Alyssa Chen: good question. Most INT8 regressions are minor paraphrase shifts and occasional tokenization artifacts, but there are corner cases where entity substitution happens. We show examples in the bench sheet, and we also have quality monitors in Optimize that flag regression on per-prompt-set metrics.
[17:18] Jordan Lee: we typically recommend FP8 for production if you need near-FP16 quality with some latency gains, and INT8 for aggressive cost-sensitive workloads where you accept a small quality hit and add strong eval/regression checks.
[17:31] Maria Gomez: can you do a live compare on one of our prompts? we shared a sanitized clinical exemplar earlier.
[17:37] Samir Patel: sure loading the sample now. Bear with the load, cloud warmups may cause a bit of jitter.
[17:53] [18:00] Samir Patel: OK here's the baseline FP16 run — generation time 1.9s for 512 tokens, output shown.
[18:08] [18:10] Samir Patel: same prompt FP8 run — generation time 1.5s, outputs look almost identical, minor paraphrase.
[18:20] [18:23] Samir Patel: now INT8 run — 0.75s generation time, output has one swapped medication name (obvious synthetic example), we'll mark that as a quality fail.
[18:33] Maria Gomez: interesting, so roughly half the latency at INT8 but with some token-level errors.
[18:39] Ethan Zhao: what's the CPU/GPU memory delta? will INT8 reduce footprint to allow more replicas per GPU?
[18:45] Samir Patel: yes INT8 quant reduces model memory by ~45% in our pipeline, so you can often pack 2x instances on the same GPU. FP8 gives ~25% reduction. Practical impact: cost per token goes down but quality monitoring must be tighter.
[18:58] Priya Raman: how does Redwood Optimize decide when to route to FP8 vs INT8? is that manual policy or automated?
[19:05] Alyssa Chen: both. We offer rules-based routing (latency SLO, cost cap, region), and an auto-recommendation engine that suggests quantization profiles based on eval results and traffic patterns. You can do gradual rollouts: canary INT8 for 5% traffic with A/B quality checks, then widen if safe.
[19:25] Luke Turner: does that require private deployment? can we do this with Hosted API?
[19:31] Jordan Lee: both — Hosted supports profile routing but Dedicated gives you stronger isolation and predictable throughput for pilots. For regulated PHI workloads we usually recommend Dedicated or Private deployment with KMS integration.
[19:47] Maria Gomez: security question — how are logs and tokens stored? do you have SOC2 scope for Dedicated?
[19:53] Jordan Lee: yes we have SOC2 for the platform; Dedicated includes isolated storage and optional KMS/HSM integration. We'll send the SOC2 and architecture diagram post-call.
[20:06] Ethan Zhao: about eval harness, can we bring our own metrics? like custom F1 for entity extraction?
[20:11] Samir Patel: absolutely, Optimize supports custom metric plug-ins and you can upload labeled sets. The autop-run will produce per-profile diffs.
[20:21] Maria Gomez: can we test an FP8 model with our ensemble pipeline? we do post-generation entity checks and fallbacks today.
[20:28] Alyssa Chen: that's actually a great fit — you can use FP8 inline for generation and then run your postcheck. If it fails, the routing policy can call FP16 fallback or trigger a synchronous high-quality path.
[20:42] Luke Turner: what's the expected cost delta? even rough numbers help for our finance team.
[20:47] Jordan Lee: rough ballpark—if INT8 gives 2.5x throughput improvement you could see 30–50% cost reduction depending on your batching. FP8 is usually 15–25% cost savings vs FP16. We'll share more precise per-token estimates for your workload.
[21:05] Samir Patel: one more note on latency: p95 improvements depend on batching and cache hit rates. For short prompts, INT8 helps less because overhead dominates, but for 512+ token runs INT8 shines.
[21:22] Priya Raman: are there regulatory flags for quantization? any audits needed for model changes?
[21:27] Jordan Lee: we log model version, quant profile, and eval outputs. For audits you can export the logs and metrics—this is part of the Dedicated compliance package.
[21:38] Maria Gomez: ok let's talk pilot scope — we want 2 weeks of daily runs on Dedicated, a seeded set of 5k prompts, and the ability to roll back automatically.
[21:48] Jordan Lee: sounds good. Samir, can you run a reproducible bench that we can hand to them?
[21:53] Samir Patel: yes I'll run the repro and upload the raw logs and bench sheet. I'll also include examples of failure modes and recommended prompts to monitor.
[22:02] [22:05] Jordan Lee: action items recap: Samir to run repro, Jordan to share pricing and SOC2, Maria to provide prompts. Any other questions?
[22:12] Maria Gomez: one last question: do you support mixed-precision within the same request? like FP8 for most tokens but INT8 for some layers?
[22:20] Alyssa Chen: we have experimental mixed precision profiles but it's nuanced—often model architecture needs tuning. We can include it as an advanced POC item but not as a default.
[22:31] Luke Turner: fine, include it as optional.
[22:35] Jordan Lee: great. We'll send the bench spreadsheet, pilot agreement draft, and security docs. Thanks everyone.
[22:42] Maria Gomez: thanks, appreciate it.
[22:45] (call ends)
